restoration_note: Teaching frames the Wheel (cyclic purification) turning within the heavens (the Five Wells / summonses stretched from winds to earth) without cleaving or mingling, because the heavens are pneumatic. Most gaps are editor's micro-restorations of partial words bound by traces (single letters, plural endings, qualitatives), all of which the apparatus already constrains tightly and the spiritual reading confirms. The one substantive medium lacuna ({2}, ~9 chars) is reconstructed as a prepositional phrase modifying ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('in the whole of the'), giving the question its standard cosmic framing — fitting the character count and the chapter's image of the Wheel coursing through the entire cosmic order. The title-fill ({0}) confirms the editor's 'Wheel and Heavens' from visible ⲡⲧⲣ and the surviving body of the chapter.

restorations.basis: Visible trace ⲡⲧⲣ requires ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ. The whole surviving body of the chapter (lines 3-23) treats precisely the relation of Wheel and heavens: 'How does the Wheel turn upon the heavens... is it that the heavens do not mingle inward with the Wheel.' Editor's restoration confirmed by the spiritual arc and lexical anchors (ⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ = wheel/cyclic process; ⲛⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ = the Five Wells/heavens-as-summonses).
Standard Kephalaia heading layout: chapter-number marker 40 (ⲙⲫ) opens and closes the title. The opening ⲙⲫ is preserved at section 3026; the closing repetition is conventional.

Est. 9 chars. The phrase 'as it turns and as it courses [...] cosmos' needs a prepositional bridge to ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ({3}). ⲍⲙ ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ ⲙⲡ ('in the whole of the') = exactly 9 chars and matches the chapter's framing of the Wheel coursing through the totality of the heavens (winds to earth). Coheres with the spiritual arc: the cyclic process passes through the entire cosmic system without cleaving it. Alternatives like ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛ ⲍⲙ ⲡ ('downward in the') are possible but less idiomatic with ⲥⲓⲧⲉ ('course/run').
Editor's restoration; only initial ⲕ is lost, with -ⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ visible. Lexicon entry confirms ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ = the present mingled-state arena, the proper sphere through which the Wheel turns.
Single-letter restoration completing ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ ('them'), the object of ⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ ('casting'), referring to the lions parted by the figurehead. Trace and grammar both binding.

Plural ending of ⲙ̄ⲙⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲉ ('lions'), with ⲙⲙⲟⲩ- visible and the English already glossing 'separating the lions'. Lexicon: ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲓ̈ = lion (dominating force, here the natural's surging dominions parted by the doctrinal ship).
Single-letter restoration completing ⲡⲉϩⲕⲟⲟⲍ ('his figurehead/corner-place'), already attested in line 10 (ⲡⲕⲟⲟⲍ ⲉⲧⲥⲁⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲧ ⲍⲙ ⲡⲧⲁⲡ, 'the figurehead set at the head'). Same lexeme; only final ⲍ lost.

Editor's reading of qualitative ⲉⲧϫⲱⲧ ('which is stretched/extended') from visible ⲉⲧϫ-. Coheres with the figurehead 'set at the head, at the front of the ship' as the extending point that parts the lions. Coptic grammar (relative + qualitative) and traces both fit.

Single-letter restoration at line beginning. The following ⲛⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ ('at that very hour') is a temporal adverbial phrase, and ⲉ- typically initiates such circumstantials in Lycopolitan. Editor's reading accepted on traces and grammar.

Editor's restoration completing ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ̄ ('joined/mingled together'), lexicon entry confirmed. The lions rejoin upon the head of the ship after the prow has passed — the chapter's central correspondential picture: the parted natural rejoins itself at once. ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ̄ is the very lemma (Mingling) used in the lexicon.

Editor's restoration completing ⲍⲱⲱⲩ ('themselves'), reflexive emphatic referring to ⲛ̄ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ ('the heavens'). Split across line break from ⲍⲱ at end of line 22. Grammar (ⲍⲱⲱⲩ + plural antecedent) and traces binding. Closes the chapter's conclusion: nor do the heavens themselves mingle inward with the Wheel.
